clue.text: Carbon or nitrogen as the result of pressure? (4)

blocks.note: c is the chemical symbol for carbon
the little joining word is taken at face value and hands over its own two letters
n is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lesson question about which element you get by squeezing something hard enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze carbon hard and you get a diamond, which is the answer the surface is offering; the real pressure here is a tight shoe on a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is the hard patch a tight shoe raises by pressing on one spot, so it is literally what pressure produces.

clue.text: Unbecoming in most of battle: a sharp punch (5,3)

indicators.note: taking most of a word means taking all of it bar the final letter

blocks.note: the preposition is used for its own letters
a battle is a fray, shortened by the instruction before it

explanation.surface: A scrap in which somebody throws an unsporting jab while most of the battle is still going on.
explanation.walkthrough: INFRA DIG is short for the Latin infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity, which is why a phrase about rank ends up meaning bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig means beneath one's dignity, which is what 'unbecoming' says of conduct that does not suit the person.

clue.text: Nutritious fruit mostly very good? Excellent (4)

indicators.note: mostly a word is the word with its final letter left off

excellent is A1, and the numeral one is written as the letter I

explanation.walkthrough: A1 written out as AI is a standing crossword trick, since the figure 1 and a capital I look the same. The berry is the Brazilian palm fruit sold everywhere as a superfood.
explanation.definitionFit: ACAI is the Brazilian palm berry marketed as a superfood, so 'nutritious fruit' names it by the selling point.

clue.text: New head of company is human so far (8)

the head of a word is the letter standing at the front of it

clue.text: Children’s writer reduced home a small amount (6)

explanation.walkthrough: E Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and Five Children and It, and her surname is one every solver eventually meets. 'Home' wants to be a house and is a nest.

clue.text: Tedium of the French lines on Spanish city, ignoring a mention of Spain (10)

indicators.note: in a down entry one thing sits on another by being written above it, so this piece goes first
to ignore a letter is to leave it out of the word it came from

blocks.note: du is how a French speaker says 'of the'
l stands for line, and the plural doubles it

explanation.surface: French lines drawn up outside a Spanish city, with Spain itself politely left unmentioned.

explanation.definitionFit: DULLSVILLE is slang for a state or place where nothing happens, which is tedium given the shape of a town name.

clue.text: Takes careful steps in board game, losing last piece (6)

explanation.walkthrough: To inch is to move by tiny degrees, a verb made out of the measurement. The pun is on 'piece', which the surface offers as a chessman and the wordplay wants as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move a little at a time, so 'takes careful steps' is that verb in its third-person form.

clue.text: Trivial hackneyed stuff after spicy stuff (10)

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective comes from British leases: a peppercorn rent is a token payment of one peppercorn a year, so peppercorn means nominal, not worth counting.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppercorn rent is a nominal one, and that legal use gives PEPPERCORN the adjective sense 'trivial'.

clue.text: Irrelevant old female never against series (2,2,11)

blocks.note: o = old, the standard abbreviation
f = female, as on a form
never is the flat refusal, no
con is against, as in the pros and cons
a sequence is a series of things in order

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who was never opposed to the series.
explanation.walkthrough: Five separate pieces stack up here, and the first two are single letters, which is what makes a fifteen-letter answer buildable at all. CON for against comes from the pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no consequence has no bearing on the matter in hand, which is exactly what calling it irrelevant says.

clue.text: Marine worms, source of each one collected by 26s (7)

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, meaning its opening letter
something collected by a group ends up held inside it

the source, that is the first letter, of 'each'
i is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.definitionFit: Nereids are the ragworms that burrow in tidal mud, so 'marine worms' is their plain zoological label.

clue.text: Hotel worker with a lot of guts taking on hotel work (7)

clue.text: Rioting led unrest in the final analysis (3,6)

explanation.definitionFit: The final analysis and the END RESULT both name what a process comes down to once everything has been weighed up.

clue.text: Nonsense that is involved in change, sapping power and enthusiasm (10)

clue.text: Last blokes to accept attention and bit of touching affectionate banter (10)

blokes are men
the first letter of 'touching'

explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is a word spoken out of fondness — darling, love, pet — which is the affectionate end of banter.
